second_order: Rallying people to keep the U alive
theme_note: These passages all recruit or stiffen collective defense of the U: the opening calls for help, later warnings name things getting dicey or an attempted takeover, and replies range from widening the mark to bluntly rejecting the takeover. They share the practice of rallying defenders, not merely the word U or their adjacency.

second_order: Keeping the U up around everyday life
theme_note: People turn spare attention, battery, class, work reading, lunch breaks, and the last hours into maintenance, then recognize even three squares as help. What varies is the amount and setting of the work; what holds it together is fitting upkeep into ordinary time.

second_order: Working out how and where to move the U
theme_note: These turns jointly work through relocation and reshaping: relaying that a move is happening, asking what will occupy the space, proposing a route and width, judging the existing orange, and proposing coordinated movement. Agreement varies, but each turn contributes to the practical plan.

Across separate exchanges, people try to coexist with nearby works: considering a truce, offering a model and maintenance help, warning the Utah U, asking Miami to stop short, accepting those requests, reporting the agreed border, and greeting as neighbors. The direction varies between asking, offering, warning, agreeing, and greeting; the shared practice is making room together rather than simply naming other subreddits.

second_order: Explaining the huge pixel board to someone who does not get it
theme_note: A newcomer asks what is happening, another person explains the board and five-minute interval, and the newcomer acknowledges it. The shared practice is giving and receiving an explanation, with each code retaining its distinct turn.

second_order: Finding a community growing around the little U
theme_note: One speaker doubts the sub can sustain the mark, then retracts that doubt on seeing it present; another celebrates a formerly two-person effort gaining a community. The passages differ in stance but together register the discovery that more people have gathered around the U.

second_order: Saving and celebrating the U surviving
theme_note: The thread first saves an image against possible loss and, once editing closes, celebrates survival, praises the defense, and calls the finish practically unscathed. The practice develops from precautionary preservation to an ending account, rather than treating all positive language as one mood.

second_order: Working out whether different colors meant a takeover
theme_note: This single code belongs with no other practice: after the event, one participant tries to interpret whether observed color changes were takeover or blocking.
